source_text: δι' ἑτέρας γραφῆς τὴν λύσιν παρέσχετο. 18.25 Ἡ δὲ νέα οὔκετι ὡς ἐν σκιᾷ καὶ παραπετάσματι, ἀλλὰ σαφῶς καὶ διαρρήδην φράζει, ὡς μαρτυροῦσιν οὗτοι· 18.26 Παῦλος γράφων Ῥωμαίοις μέν· «εἴπερ εἷς ὁ θεός», Γαλάταις δὲ καὶ Κορινθίοις· «ὁ θεὸς εἷς ἐστιν». 18.27 Καὶ πάλιν δὲ Κορινθίοις τὸ δεύτερον· «ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἡ κοι νωνία τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν». 18.28 ἐνταῦθα διὰ τὸ ταὐτὸν τῆς θεότητος πρώτου ἐμνημόνευσεν τοῦ υἱοῦ, καὶ οὕτω τοῦ πατρός, εἶτα τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος αὐτοῦ. 18.29 κοινωνίαν δὲ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος μετὰ πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ εἶπεν τῆς μιᾶς θεότητος καὶ δόξης καὶ βασιλείας. ποία γὰρ ἄλλη ἐπὶ θεοῦ κοινωνία; 18.30 Ἐφεσίοις δέ· «εἷς κύριος, μία πίστις, ἓν βάπτισμα, εἷς θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ πάντων, ὁ ἐπὶ πάν των καὶ διὰ πάντων καὶ ἐν πᾶσιν». εἶτα τοῖς αὐτοῖς· «τούτου χάριν κάμπτω τὰ γόνατά μου πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ πατέρα, ἐξ οὗ πᾶσα πατριὰ ἐν οὐρανοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς ὀνομάζεται, ἵνα δῷ ὑμῖν κατὰ τὸν πλοῦτον τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ δυνάμει κραταιωθῆναι διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον κατοικῆσαι τὸν Χριστὸν διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις». 18.31 Ὧδε πάλιν ὁμοίως διὰ τὸ ἰσότιμον τῶν ὑποστάσεων μετὰ τὸν πατέρα πρώτου τοῦ πνεύματος καὶ οὕτω τοῦ υἱοῦ ἐμνημόνευσεν. 18.32 Καὶ πάλιν Κορινθίοις· «παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, διὰ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ διὰ τῆς ἀγάπης τοῦ πνεύματος, συναγωνίσασθαί μοι ἐν ταῖς προσευχαῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ πρὸς τὸν θεόν». 18.33 Ἑβραίοις δέ· «εἰ γὰρ ὁ δι' ἀγγέλων λαληθεὶς λόγος ἐγένετο βέβαιος, καὶ πᾶσα παράβασις καὶ παρακοὴ ἔλαβεν ἔνδικον μισθαποδοσίαν, πῶς ἡμεῖς ἐκφευξόμεθα τηλικαύτης ἀμελήσαντες σωτηρίας; ἥτις ἀρχὴν λαβοῦσα λαλεῖσθαι διὰ τοῦ κυρίου, ὑπὸ τῶν ἀκουσάντων εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐβεβαιώθη, συνεπιμαρτυροῦντος τοῦ θεοῦ σημείοις τε καὶ τέρασιν καὶ ποικίλαις δυνάμεσιν καὶ πνεύματος ἁγίου μερισμοῖς κατὰ τὴν αὐτοῦ θέλησιν». 18.34 ∆ιὰ οὖν τοῦ κυρίου δεδήλωται ὁ υἱός, διὰ δὲ τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ πατήρ, εἶτα καὶ τὸ αὐτεξούσιον καὶ παντοδύναμον τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος. 18.35 Καὶ ὁ υἱὸς δὲ ἔδειξεν τὴν μὲν μίαν θεότητα διὰ τοῦ εἰπεῖν· «τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν; οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός», τὰς δὲ ἰσοτίμους καὶ ἰσοδυνάμους τρεῖς ὑποστάσεις διὰ τῆς περὶ τὸ βάπτισμα διδαχῆς. 18.36 μὴ εἰπὼν δὲ πειραστικῶς ἐξετάσαντι τῷ νομικῷ· μή με λέγε ἀγαθόν, ἀλλά· «τί με λέγεις ἀγαθόν;», ἔδειξεν ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ἀγαθός ἐστιν ἐν ἴσῳ τῷ πατρί, καὶ ἐκ τῆς πατρικῆς ἀγαθότητος ἐκφαίνεται ἡ αὐτοῦ, καὶ δείκνυται ἀπὸ ἀγαθοῦ ἀγαθὸς γεγεννημένος. 18.37 «εἰ γάρ», φησίν, «οἶδάς με ἀγαθόν, καὶ μὴ συμπλέκεις τῷ διδασκάλῳ τὴν λέξιν» ὡς τό· «εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθέ», καὶ ὡς «ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ τῆς καρδίας προφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν», καὶ ὡς «ἀγαθὸς ἦν Σαμουὴλ μετὰ θεοῦ καὶ ἀνθρώπων», καί· «ἀγαθὸς ἦν Σαούλ, υἱὸς Κὶς ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμίν, ὑψηλότερος παντὸς Ἰσραὴλ ὑπὲρ ὠμίαν καὶ ἐπάνω», καί· «ἀγαθὸς κύων ὁ ζῶν ὑπὲρ τὸν λέοντα τὸν τεθνηκότα». «Μηδὲν παραιροῦ τοῦ πρωτουργοῦ ἀγαθοῦ, ἀλλ' ὡς θεόν με ἐπίγνωθι, μὴ ἄλλον τῇ θεότητι 19 τοῦ πατρός, ἀλλὰ τῇ ὑποστάσει». 18.38 μία γὰρ ἡ ἀμφοτέρων θεότης· ἐπεὶ οὐκέτι τὸ πρῶτον ἀγαθὸν ἓν εὑρίσκεται. «ἀνέγνως γάρ που», φησίν, «ὡς «ἀγαθόν σοι πεποιθέναι ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον ἢ πεποιθέναι ἐπ' ἄνθρωπον». «τὸ γὰρ προσκολλᾶσθαι τῷ θεῷ ἀγαθόν ἐστιν». καὶ ὡς ἀγαθῷ ἀκολουθεῖν μοι καὶ κατόπιν μου βαίνειν ὑμᾶς ἀεὶ προέτρεψα». 18.39 ∆ιὸ οὐκ εἶπεν μέν· «οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ πατήρ», ἀλλ' «οὐδεὶς ἀγαθὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός», ὡς καὶ ἐν ἄλλῳ που λέγει· «τί με λέγετε κύριε κύριε καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους;» 18.40 ἡ γὰρ κτίσις, φησίν, κατὰ μετοχὴν τὴν ἀγαθότητα ἔχει, ἀπομιμουμένη πρὸς δύναμιν τὴν ἑαυτῆς, εἰ θέμις εἰπεῖν, τὴν ἔμφυτον καὶ τελείαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἀγαθότητα καὶ δι' αὐτῆς σωζομένη. καὶ ἔστιν ὕπαρξις τοῦ ἐν αὐτῇ ἀγαθοῦ τὸ μετέχειν τῆς τοῦ θεοῦ, προσκολλωμένην αὐτῷ τῇ ὑπακοῇ καὶ τῷ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἔρωτι. 18.41 ἐγράφη γὰρ ὡς «οἱ μακρύνοντες ἑαυτοὺς ἀπὸ σοῦ ἀπολοῦνται», καί· «μακρὰν ἀπέχει ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ ἀσεβῶν», καὶ «μακρὰν ἀπὸ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἡ σωτηρία». 18.42 δῆλον δέ, ὡς σχέσει καὶ διαθέσει διὰ τὴν πρὸς τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐναντίωσιν καὶ τὸ πρὸς ἀρετὴν βράδος, ἀλλ' οὐ τόπῳ. 18.43 Ὅτι δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς ἀγαθός ἐστιν, ἅτε φύσει τῷ ἀγαθῷ πατρὶ ὑπάρχων ἕν, αὐτός τε ἐν Ματθαίῳ λέγει· «ἢ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρός ἐστιν, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀγαθός εἰμι;» καὶ πάλιν· «Μαρία τὴν ἀγαθὴν μερίδα ἐξελέξατο, ἥτις οὐκ ἀφαιρεθήσεται ἀπ' αὐτῆς.» ἔλεγεν δέ «ἀγαθὴν μερίδα»
pass_a_gloss: [...] through another Scripture it furnished the solution. 18.25 But the new [covenant] no longer as in shadow and curtain, but clearly and expressly declares, as these bear witness: 18.26 Paul, writing to the Romans on the one hand: 'since God is one', and to Galatians and Corinthians on the other: 'God is one'. 18.27 And again to Corinthians the second time: 'the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the communion of the Holy Spirit with all of you'. 18.28 Here on account of the sameness of the Godhead he made mention of the Son first, and so of the Father, then of his Holy Spirit. 18.29 And he spoke of a communion of the Holy Spirit with Father and Son of the one Godhead and glory and kingdom. For what other communion [is there] in the case of God? 18.30 And to Ephesians: 'one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, the one over all and through all and in all'. Then to the same: 'for the sake of this I bend my knees toward the God and Father, out of whom every family in heavens and on earth is named, so that he may give you according to the wealth of his glory to be made strong with power through his Spirit into the inner man, that Christ dwell through the faith in the hearts'. 18.31 Here again likewise on account of the equal honour of the hypostases, after the Father he made mention first of the Spirit and so of the Son. 18.32 And again to Corinthians: 'and I exhort you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to contend together with me in the prayers on my behalf toward God'. 18.33 And to Hebrews: 'for if the word spoken through angels became firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just repayment, how shall we escape, having neglected so great a salvation? which, having taken a beginning to be spoken through the Lord, was made firm into us by those who heard, God bearing witness together with signs and wonders and varied powers and distributions of Holy Spirit according to his will'. 18.34 So through 'the Lord' the Son has been made plain, and through 'God' the Father, then also the self-determining and all-powerful [character] of the Holy Spirit. 18.35 And the Son too showed on the one hand the one Godhead through saying: 'why do you call me good? no one is good except one, God', and on the other the three hypostases of equal honour and equal power through the teaching about baptism. 18.36 And not having said to the lawyer who examined him testingly: do not call me good, but: 'why do you call me good?', he showed that he himself too is good on an equal footing with the Father, and out of the paternal goodness his own shines forth, and he is shown as begotten good from good. 18.37 'For if', he says, 'you know me good, and do not entwine the word with the teacher', as the [saying]: 'well, good slave', and as 'the good man out of the good treasure of the heart brings forward the good', and as 'Samuel was good with God and men', and: 'Saul was good, son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin, taller than all Israel from shoulder and upward', and: 'good is the living dog beyond the lion that has died'. 'Take away nothing from the first-working Good, but recognise me as God, not other than the Father in Godhead, but in hypostasis'. 18.38 For one is the Godhead of both; since [otherwise] the first Good is no longer found one. 'For you have read somewhere', he says, 'that it is good for you to have trusted in the Lord rather than to have trusted in man. For to cling to God is good. And I always urged you to follow me as good and to walk behind me'. 18.39 Therefore he did not say: 'no one is good except one, the Father', but 'no one is good except one, God', as also somewhere in another place he says: 'why do you call me Lord, Lord, and do not do my words?' 18.40 For the creation, he says, has goodness according to participation, imitating according to its own power, if it is right to say, the inborn and perfect goodness of God and being kept safe through it. And the existence of the good in it is the sharing in that of God, [it] clinging to him by obedience and by love toward him. 18.41 For it was written that 'those who make themselves far from you will perish', and: 'God stands far off from the ungodly', and 'far from sinners is salvation'. 18.42 And it is plain that [this is] by relation and disposition, on account of the opposition toward the good and the slowness toward virtue, but not by place. 18.43 And that he himself too is good, as being one by nature with the good Father, he himself both says in Matthew: 'or is your eye evil because I am good?' and again: 'Mary chose the good portion, which will not be taken away from her'. And he was saying 'good portion' [...]
pass_b_english: … it has supplied the solution through another Scripture. The New Testament, however, no longer speaks as in a shadow and behind a veil, but clearly and in so many words, as these witnesses show.

Paul writes to the Romans, “Since God is one” (Romans 3:30), and to the Galatians and the Corinthians, “God is one” (Galatians 3:20). And again to the Corinthians, in the second letter: “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all” (2 Corinthians 13:14). Here, because the Godhead is the same, he mentioned the Son first, then the Father, and then his Holy Spirit. And he spoke of the communion of the Holy Spirit with the Father and the Son: a communion in the one Godhead, glory and kingdom. For what other communion could there be in God?

To the Ephesians he writes: “One Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all, who is over all and through all and in all” (Ephesians 4:5-6). Then to the same readers: “For this reason I bend my knees to the God and Father, from whom every family in the heavens and on earth is named, that he may grant you, according to the riches of his glory, to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in the inner man, so that Christ may dwell in the hearts through faith” (Ephesians 3:14-17). Here again, in the same way, because the hypostases are equal in honour, he mentioned the Spirit first after the Father, and then the Son.
And again to the Corinthians: “I urge you, brothers, through our Lord Jesus Christ and through the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in your prayers to God for me” (Romans 15:30).

And to the Hebrews: “For if the word spoken through angels proved firm, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense, how shall we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It began to be spoken through the Lord, and it was confirmed to us by those who heard him, while God bore witness with them by signs and wonders and various mighty works, and by distributions of the Holy Spirit according to his will” (Hebrews 2:2-4). By “the Lord”, then, the Son is made known; by “God”, the Father; and then also the Holy Spirit, free in his own will and almighty.

The Son too showed the one Godhead by saying, “Why do you call me good? No one is good but one, God” (Mark 10:18); and he showed the three hypostases, equal in honour and equal in power, by his teaching on baptism (Matthew 28:19). To the lawyer who questioned him to test him he did not say, “Do not call me good,” but, “Why do you call me good?” So he showed that he himself is good, equally with the Father; that his own goodness shines out from the Father’s goodness; and that he is good, begotten of the Good.

“For if,” he says, “you know me to be good, and are not tying the word to ‘teacher’ as in ‘Well done, good servant’ (Matthew 25:21), and ‘The good man brings out good from the good treasure of his heart’ (Luke 6:45), and ‘Samuel was good with God and with men’ (1 Samuel 2:26), and ‘Saul, son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin, was good, taller than all Israel from the shoulders upward’ (1 Samuel 9:1-2), and ‘Good is the living dog, above the lion that is dead’ (Ecclesiastes 9:4), then take nothing away from the primal Good. Acknowledge me as God: not other than the Father in Godhead, but in hypostasis.”

For the Godhead of the two is one; otherwise the first Good would no longer be found to be one. “For you have read somewhere,” he says, “that ‘it is good for you to trust in the Lord rather than to trust in man’ (Psalm 118:8), and ‘to cling to God is good’ (Psalm 73:28); and I have always urged you to follow me as good and to walk behind me.” That is why he did not say, “No one is good but one, the Father,” but, “No one is good but one, God,” just as he says somewhere else, “Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do my words?” (Luke 6:46).

For creation, he says, has its goodness by participation. It imitates as far as it can, if one may say so, the innate and perfect goodness of God, and is preserved by it. The very existence of the good in creation is its sharing in God’s goodness, as it clings to him by obedience and by love for him. For it is written, “Those who remove themselves far from you will perish” (Psalm 73:27), and, “God is far from the ungodly” (Proverbs 15:29), and, “Salvation is far from sinners” (Psalm 119:155). Plainly this distance is one of relation and disposition, caused by opposition to the good and slowness toward virtue, and not one of place.

That he too is good, since by nature he is one with the good Father, he himself says in Matthew: “Or is your eye evil because I am good?” (Matthew 20:15); and again: “Mary has chosen the good portion, which shall not be taken away from her” (Luke 10:42). And he said “the good portion” …

lemmas.gloss: self-determining, free in one's own will

choices.issue: Old draft a digest with labels and fillers
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed the edition numbers 18.36-18.43 as paragraph openers ('In 18.36, …'), added a sentence that is not in the Greek ('The argument continues through the teaching regarding baptism'), broke 18.35 off at '[and] the three equal and equal-powered [hypostases]...', and used bracket fillers [writing], [thing], [and], [hypostases]. Garbled clauses fixed: 18.27 τὸ δεύτερον ('the second [thing]': it means the second letter); 18.34 (the Spirit's self-determination was made a third thing 'revealed'); 18.37 ('do not entangle the teacher with the word', 'do not withdraw from the primary Good', 'not another in the divinity of the Father'); 18.38 ('it was once read'); 18.40 (the clinging is creation's, not God's); 18.42 βράδος ('degree': it means slowness). References: all abbreviations written in full; Ephesians 4:4-6 narrowed to 4:5-6 (the quotation starts at 'one Lord'); Ephesians 3:16-17 widened to 3:14-17; Luke 19:17 replaced by Matthew 25:21 (Didymus has εὖ, Matthew's word); Luke 9:23 removed (only a possible echo, listed as Matthew 16:24); 1 Corinthians 8:6 moved to a possible allusion; Psalm 73:28 and Matthew 28:19 added; 1 Samuel 9:2 widened to 9:1-2 (Kish and Benjamin are in verse 1).

choices.term: δι' ἑτέρας γραφῆς τὴν λύσιν παρέσχετο
choices.english: … it has supplied the solution through another Scripture
choices.why: The section opens in the middle of a sentence begun in the previous section (the Old Testament often explains a hard passage by another). Only these words are translated, with a leading ellipsis.
Feminine adjective answering ἡ παλαιὰ διαθήκη in the previous section; 'Testament' is the noun English needs, so no brackets.

choices.term: τὸ αὐτεξούσιον καὶ παντοδύναμον τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος
choices.english: the Holy Spirit, free in his own will and almighty
choices.why: Didymus draws this from 'according to his will' (Hebrews 2:4): the Spirit distributes gifts by his own will. αὐτεξούσιος is self-determining.

choices.term: διὰ τῆς περὶ τὸ βάπτισμα διδαχῆς
choices.why: The baptismal command in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit; a clear allusion, so it is cited.

choices.term: «εἰ γάρ», φησίν, «οἶδάς με ἀγαθόν, καὶ μὴ συμπλέκεις τῷ διδασκάλῳ τὴν λέξιν» ὡς τό …
choices.english: “For if,” he says, “you know me to be good, and are not tying the word to ‘teacher’ as in …
choices.why: Didymus voices Christ's reply to the man who said 'Good teacher': if 'good' is meant in the full sense and not in the ordinary human sense of the five examples, then acknowledge him as God. The copy-text's quotation marks break the speech in two; English keeps it as one speech, with the conditional finished by 'then take nothing away'.

choices.term: ἀγαθὸς κύων ὁ ζῶν ὑπὲρ τὸν λέοντα τὸν τεθνηκότα
choices.english: Good is the living dog, above the lion that is dead
choices.why: Ecclesiastes 9:4 normally reads 'better than'; the word 'good' is kept because Didymus cites the verse for that word.
The Good that is first and source of all goodness, as against goodness by participation in 18.40.

choices.term: μὴ ἄλλον τῇ θεότητι τοῦ πατρός, ἀλλὰ τῇ ὑποστάσει
choices.english: not other than the Father in Godhead, but in hypostasis
choices.why: The dative of respect marks where the Son is other than the Father (hypostasis) and where he is not (Godhead).

choices.term: ἐπεὶ οὐκέτι τὸ πρῶτον ἀγαθὸν ἓν εὑρίσκεται
choices.english: otherwise the first Good would no longer be found to be one
choices.why: ἐπεί with an implied unreal condition: if the Godhead of the two were not one, there would be two first Goods.
Here of creation kept in being by God's goodness, not saving grace.

choices.term: σχέσει καὶ διαθέσει … ἀλλ' οὐ τόπῳ
choices.english: a distance of relation and disposition … and not one of place
choices.why: Didymus explains 'far from God' in 18.41: the distance is moral, not spatial.
Quotations from the Greek Psalter; English numbers used in the references.
The section ends mid-sentence; the explanation follows in the next section. Ends with '…'.

choices.term: κοι νωνία; πάν των; θεότητι 19 τοῦ πατρός
choices.why: Words split by line breaks in the copy-text are read as single words; the printed number 19 inside 18.37 is page debris and is skipped.
